summary: Connect a vector-output dense–ReLU layer and all its gradients to an actual TorchLean graph and automatically generated backward.

Verify a separately supplied parallel binary32 forward implementation with a fixed reduction tree and fresh scratch in one bounded cooperating thread array; prove a complete admitted execution whose stored outputs approximate the actual TorchLean real graph under explicit encoding and range conditions, while distinguishing correctness for all admitted executions.

For arbitrary candidate forward traces, prove strict per-thread instruction order, classify every emitted store site and derive timing around observed barrier completions; computed-address ownership and universal stored-output correctness remain open.
remaining: Implemented: actual TorchLean matrix graph and generated VJP; balanced-tree numerical bounds; the shape-specialized forward instruction list and complete selected execution through every reduction round, barrier, bias/ReLU output store and thread exit; derived stored reference words, unchanged inputs, preserved extents and full-trace access safety. The same trace has a proved graph admission certificate, using derived read sources, chronological write ordering and actual barrier edges, with no circular order/read-source chain. Its stored words approximate the actual TorchLean real tensor graph under explicit entry-encoding and calculated finite-range conditions; zero-padding removal and the tensor/tree identity are proved, including empty inputs. Arbitrary candidate traces now have strict per-thread instruction order, at-most-once execution of each store site, exhaustive emitted-store site classification and timing derived around observed completed barriers. Missing: computed-address ownership and existence of each required producer and phase in arbitrary completed executions, the resulting read-source and arithmetic-tree correspondence, and universal stored numerical correspondence; an empty-output no-launch wrapper; and the parallel backward kernel and its proofs. No desired load values, intermediate accuracy, tensor/tree identity or memory validity are assumed by the selected execution proof.

The layer takes an input vector x of length n, a trainable m-by-n weight matrix W,
and a bias vector b of length m. It returns y_i=max(sum_j W_ij*x_j+b_i,0).
Its automatically generated TorchLean backward takes an incoming sensitivity
vector d of length m. With g_i=d_i on a positive affine value and zero otherwise,
it returns dx_j=sum_i W_ij*g_i, dW_ij=g_i*x_j and db_i=g_i. A zero derivative at
an exactly zero affine value is a chosen convention; ordinary mathematical
differentiation requires every relevant affine value to be nonzero.

structure Encoding (s : Dense.Shape) (global : List Word)
    (x : Tensor ℝ (DenseVJP.column s.columns))
    (w : Tensor ℝ (DenseVJP.matrix s.rows s.columns))
    (b : Tensor ℝ (DenseVJP.column s.rows)) where
  entry : Fin s.rows → Fin s.columns → DotError.Input
  weightWord : ∀ r c, (entry r c).left = global[s.weight r.val c.val]!
  inputWord : ∀ r c, (entry r c).right = global[c.val]!
  weightIdeal : ∀ r c, (entry r c).l = Spec.get2 w r c
  inputIdeal : ∀ r c, (entry r c).r = Spec.get2 x c 0
  biasValue : Fin s.rows → ℝ
  biasError : Fin s.rows → ℝ
  biasReal : ∀ r, finiteReal global[s.biasBase+r.val]! = some (biasValue r)
  biasApprox : ∀ r, |biasValue r-Spec.get2 b r 0| ≤ biasError r
  treeSafe : ∀ r, Reduction.Safe (Reduction.balanced s.depth 0 (Reduction.paddedInput (entry r)))
  additionRange : ∀ r, |Reduction.rounded (Reduction.balanced s.depth 0 (Reduction.paddedInput (entry r)))+
    biasValue r| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite
